title: Wenna's door
goals: Go through it into the corridor.
starting_code:
# Open the door with its `open` method. The door's variable goes before the dot.

# Go up two steps to pass through.
hints: Remember whose method `open` is, and what is written before the dot.
A method needs its brackets, even with nothing between them.
The object is called `door` and its method `open`: it is written `door.open()`. Once it is open, go up two steps.
intro: The doors of my library are opened by those who come to learn. As this door is not locked, you can open it simply by using its `open` method. Open it and go through into the corridor. And if it does not work the first time, remember that you can ask for a hint.
learned: Now you know that an object other than your wizard has its own methods, and that they are written after the variable that keeps it.
